$comment: GENERATED — do not edit by hand.
idea: A fitted Gaussian on its baseline reads as the letter A, and the A crossbar IS the spectrum baseline. One figure carrying both the subject and the initial, with nothing added to make the pun work.
credit: Observed by the user against candidate 05 of the retired mark-candidates sheet — the peak was drawn as a spectroscopy mark and is a better monogram than the monogram candidate.

construction.crossbar: placed where the curve reaches 0.42 of its height, so it terminates ON the flanks rather than crossing them — that contact is what makes it read as an A rather than as a peak with a line over it

cuts.name: wide
cuts.reads: a hill — spectroscopy first, letter second

cuts.name: mid
cuts.reads: both at once, which is the point

cuts.name: narrow
cuts.reads: a letter — A first, peak second

open: Which sigma, and whether the crossbar ships at all — imagery/mark-peak-*-nobar-light.svg is the control.

chosen.construction: A Gaussian over a full-width axis. sigma 13, axis at y=54 of 120, apex at y=10.
chosen.why: One line does both jobs — the x axis a peak is measured against, and the crossbar that makes the figure an A. The earlier version carried a low baseline AND a crossbar, which was one line too many: it read as a peak on a shelf with a bar across it rather than as one letter.
chosen.strokes: 4px, non-scaling, so the weight is a device pixel count and not a viewBox unit — the fault that made the first cover mark render at 13.5px against 1px hairlines.
chosen.supersedes: the three-cut sigma study and the crossbar-at-0.42 construction below
chosen.sharpened: sigma 19 -> 13 and the axis 62 -> 54. A wide peak with a low crossbar reads as a hill with a line under it; a narrow peak with a high crossbar reads as an A. The footer variant keeps its axis low because there the axis IS the page rule.
